title: Subscriber-tiered emergency mitigation and live-repair flow for model rollout deviations
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Scope: Rapid response playbook and tooling to detect, contain, and live-repair model rollout deviations that surface as customer-facing behavior regressions across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket builds a subscriber-tiered flow (per-customer priority levels) so we can apply graduated mitigations without full global rollback.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-customer-stabilization for rollout regressions to under 20 minutes for P0 subscribers.
- Provide automated rapid containment actions (routing split, model pin, param patch) plus a verified live-repair path that avoids full rollback when safe.
- Reconcile KV cache and stateful artifacts across mixed runtime planes to prevent stale-cache rehydation failures after partial fixes.
- Standardize customer communications templates and escalation handoffs between Support, SEs, and Oncall.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook runs from detection -> containment -> live-repair validated with synthetic acceptance tests within 20m in staging.
- A per-subscriber traffic-slice API that can be toggled by ops and used in the playbook.
- KV cache TTL/rehydration checklist and automated reconciliation tool that runs post-fix.
- Communication templates (initial triage, status updates, postmortem) maintained in Confluence and linked to incidents.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Live-repair operations will sometimes increase latency for affected slices; we accept brief latency increases in favor of preserving output quality for high-priority subscribers.
- Conservative default is to pin to the previously verified model if immediate fix is ambiguous. Advanced live-repair only used when synthetic and sample-based validation pass.
- Private deployments may lack automated traffic-slicing API; playbook falls back to operator-run routing changes and customer-assisted patching.

Out of scope: fully automated rollback of on-prem package upgrades and upgrading private control planes (handled by separate maintenance runbooks).

Noted gap: no per-subscriber containment path. Filed initial design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RND/Subscriber-Tiered+Mitigation+Proposal

2026-02-22 — Diego Martinez: Drafted containment API spec for 'slice-toggle' (routes traffic at the proxy layer by subscriber ID). Proto available in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-tools/pull/482

2026-02-28 — SRE Review (Liam O'Connor): Raised concerns about KV cache staleness when pinning older model binaries. Added requirement: reconciliation step must verify KV signatures and evict stale prefixes before unpinning. Marked as blocking for Dedicated flows.

2026-03-03 — Eng: Implemented traffic-slice toggle in staging and executed tabletop run. Measured worst-case containment enforcement latency 3.2s. Documented rollback fallback knobs and added tests to runtime-1.22 acceptance suite.
2026-03-06 — Product (Maya Singh): Defined customer comms templates for P0/P1/P2 tiers. Templates pushed to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RND/Customer+Escalation+Templates

2026-03-09 — Diego Martinez: Added automated KV reconciliation script (kvc-reconcile.sh) that checks per-tenant cache digests, evicts prefixes older than configured threshold, and runs synthetic rehydration probes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1217

2026-03-12 — Oncall (Hannah Xu): Performed a live drill with Support and SE to validate handoff cadence. Found a timing gap between initial triage and ops action in Private deployments; created follow-up subtask ENG-10012346 to add operator playbook for manual routing changes.
